chunk_findings.detail:
Hmm, let me assess this carefully before reporting.

The change `from ddflow import __version__ as _VERSION` relies on the package `ddflow` being importable as a top-level name at the moment `ddflow.surfaces.mcp` is imported. Since `mcp.py` is itself inside the `ddflow.surfaces` package, `ddflow` is by construction already imported (a subpackage cannot be imported without first importing its parent package), and the diff shows `ddflow/__init__.py` is just a docstring plus a single `__version__` literal, so there is no import cycle and no dependency that could fail. The value is a plain string literal, so `SERVER_INFO["version"]` remains a string. I cannot construct an input or environment in which this returns a wrong value.

Similarly, the README edits ("`ddflow/__init__.py` (the one declared version)" in the release-gate bullet, and adding `server.template.json` to the shipped-path list) are documentation and are consistent with the declared design; the shipped list already contains `ddflow/`, which includes `__init__.py`, so editing only `__init__.py` still counts as a shipped change. No functional defect is demonstrable from this hunk.

I looked specifically for the usual failure modes in a "single-source version via plain import" change — circular import between `__init__.py` and `surfaces/mcp.py`, a non-string version being injected into `SERVER_INFO`, and a stale metadata read via `importlib.metadata` — and the diff avoids all three: `__init__.py` is dependency-free, the literal is a string, and the import is a direct attribute import rather than metadata lookup. I have nothing concrete to report against this portion of the change.

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes the `uv lock` step from `scripts/bump.sh` and asserts (in the new comments in both `pyproject.toml` and `bump.sh`, and in the design notes) that "uv.lock records no version for this project." For a normal (editable/workspace-root) project, `uv.lock` carries an entry of the form `[[package]] name = "ddflow-mcp" version = "0.1.9" source = { editable = "." }`; the project's own version is part of the lock's identity, and `uv` obtains it for a dynamic-version project by resolving the project metadata (via the build backend / the hatch version source), which reads `ddflow/__init__.py`. If that is the case here, then after `scripts/bump.sh patch` the flow is: only `ddflow/__init__.py` (and the rendered `server.json`) change, while `uv.lock` still holds the previous `version`. Concretely, `uv lock --check` then reports the lock is out of date, and any CI step that uses `uv sync --locked` / `uv run` rewrites `uv.lock` — meaning the committed release tree (`release X.Y.Z`) is not the tree CI actually built from, which is precisely the failure the deleted comment ("uv.lock records the project's own version too, so it is re-locked here; left stale, the next `uv run` rewrites it…") was warning about. This needs to be verified against the actual `uv.lock` in the repo; if `uv.lock` really does contain a `version` for `ddflow-mcp`, dropping the re-lock is a regression.

chunk_findings.detail: The hand-rolled `VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][A-Za-z0-9.]+)?$")` is not PEP 440, and it is *stricter* than the rest of the toolchain it is meant to guard. It requires the pre-release/local suffix to start with `.` or `-`, so a perfectly valid version such as `__version__ = "0.2.0rc1"` fails `VERSION_RE.match`, and `declared_version()` calls `sys.exit("ddflow/__init__.py: '0.2.0rc1' is not a version")`. With that edit to the single source file, `uv build` (hatchling/`packaging`, which accept and normalize `0.2.0rc1`) would happily produce a `0.2.0rc1` wheel, but `scripts/render_server_json.py` — and therefore the CI gate/verify jobs and the "server.json is the render of the template" test — fails before server.json is written. The same applies to local versions (`0.2.0+local`). The regex is also loose in the other direction: it accepts non-PEP-440 strings such as `0.1.10.` or `1.2.3-b.`, which would be substituted verbatim into the OCI identifier tags, deferring the failure to registry publish time instead of catching it here.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_declared()` extracts the version with `re.search(r'^__version__ = "([^"]+)"$', ..., re.M)`. Python's `re.M` `$` anchors only before a `
` (or end of string); it does not treat `` as a line boundary. So on any checkout where `ddflow/__init__.py` has CRLF line endings (e.g. a Windows machine with `core.autocrlf=true`, or a tree produced by a tool that writes `
`), the line reads `__version__ = "0.1.10"
`, the position immediately after the closing `"` is followed by `` (not `
` and not end-of-string), `$` cannot match there, and `[^"]+` cannot extend past the closing quote. `m` is therefore `None` and the test aborts with `AssertionError: no __version__ literal in ddflow/__init__.py` even though the file is a perfectly valid single-literal declaration (and hatchling, which does not anchor with `$`, would still build the right version). The previous implementation (`tomllib.loads(pyproject)["project"]["version"]`) was line-ending agnostic, so this diff introduces the sensitivity. Using `[^
"]+` (or stripping the line) would avoid it.

chunk_findings.detail: The new docstring states that `SERVER_INFO` "is built from `ddflow.__version__`", and the design (intent items 1–3) requires `ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py` to obtain the version by plain import from `ddflow/__init__.py` (importlib.metadata is explicitly rejected). The sentence this same diff deletes from that docstring was the note that this is not permitted: "not `ddflow.__version__`, because the package root is not a layer `surfaces` may import (`tests/test_layering.py`)". With `__version__` still declared in `ddflow/__init__.py` (the diff keeps it there and only edits its comment), `mcp.py` must add `from ddflow import __version__` (or `import ddflow`), which is precisely the surfaces→root import `tests/test_layering.py` rejects; the change as described lists no update to `tests/test_layering.py` (the test-file work is scoped to `tests/test_packaging.py::test_the_declared_versions_agree`). Concretely: run the full suite after this change and the layering test fails, which also fails the release gate documented in the README ("the full suite ... must agree"). Either `tests/test_layering.py` needs an explicit allowance for the root's `__version__`, or `SERVER_INFO`'s version has to come from a layer the surfaces layer is allowed to import — deleting the explanatory sentence does not remove the constraint.

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard test only checks one spelling of the thing it is supposed to prevent. It asserts the literal single-quoted substring `'^version = '` is absent and that the substring `"__init__.py"` appears somewhere in each file:

```python
assert "'^version = '" not in text
assert "__init__.py" in text
```

Given `publish.yml` (or `release.sh`/`bump.sh`) that still extracts the version from `pyproject.toml` with a different quoting, e.g. `grep -m1 "^version = " pyproject.toml`, or `sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' pyproject.toml`, both assertions still hold (the double-quoted/sed spellings do not contain the single-quoted literal `'^version = '`, and the files contain the string `__init__.py` elsewhere), so the test passes. Because `pyproject.toml` now has no static `version =` line (it is `dynamic = ["version"]`), such a step yields an empty version and the workflow publishes with the wrong/empty version — exactly the regression ("the workflow would publish an empty version") that the docstring claims this test catches. The check needs to assert the actual extraction reads `ddflow/__init__.py`/`__version__`, not one exact quoting of the old grep.
